newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer amid Escondida strike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer amid Escondida strike.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer after a rangebound, lackluster session although the market was keeping one eye on developments at Escondida mine in Chile as the strike by a small group of workers continued.
May COMEX copper settled 0.40 cent firmer at 107.20 cents per pound, traded 107.40 to 105.20 cents. Spot April went out 0.10 cent higher at 107.40 cents. Volume was estimated at 6,000 lots.

Brokers said they did not expect the strike at Escondida to last long, though there were unconfirmed reports that production was already affected with the company having to consume stockpiles to maintain output levels.
The LME cash to three months backwardation widened about $20 to $60/$65 on Monday.
Later this week unions and management at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine meet in a bid to resolve stalled labor talks.
